evidence_notes: Source-based (Venus): claim = author supports Venus exploration via safety, technology, and value; three block quotes from the article (170F/sea-level pressure, silicon carbide electronics lasting three weeks, closing value passage), each tagged 'this proves/shows'. org 4 (early controlling idea, full frame, but the three supports are interchangeable - safety/tech/value could swap freely); dev 4 (quotes are specific and the connection is stated, but every explanation restates the quote rather than interpreting it, so rung 5 fails); conv 4 (spelling slips - reseachers, techonlogy, worthly, 'more safer' - visible but never require re-reading; sentence shape is formulaic, so rung 5 fails); arg 3 (position clear and committed but reasons are asserted not reasoned - never says why the quoted conditions prove safety; conclusion restates the intro almost verbatim).

Driverless cars: loosely pro position ('here to change the world'); support = Google cars driving independently since 2009, speculative benefits (gas savings, environment, watching movies), smart-road binary code idea. org 3 (controlling idea present early but the essay stops rather than closes - no closing paragraph, frame incomplete); dev 3 (Google/2009 is the one specific piece; the rest is general speculation listed with the reader supplying the connection); conv 3 (accumulating spelling errors - chang, hug, techology, bewteen, enviroment - plus run-ons and missing spaces force re-reading to repair, but meaning stays recoverable); arg 3 (position clear enough and committed, but reasons are asserted - cars 'could' save money or be safer with no why given).

Driverless cars, agrees: 'I will agree with the development of driverless cars'; supports = helps elderly/children, drivers can sleep, states beginning to legalize; concedes current safety doubts then answers with human fallibility (sleepy drivers, phone calls). org 3 (paragraph 3 repeats the elderly/children point from paragraph 2 without adding to it, and unity breaks); dev 3 (the driver-fatigue scenario is the only near-specific support; most claims - safer, more popular, more comfortable - go unsupported and are listed); conv 2 ('the new technique is shows the good way of them to serve us', fragments, safty/confutable/contrl - at least once I had to guess rather than repair); arg 4 (the safety objection is raised and answered by reasoning that computers do not tire while humans err, so a reason is genuinely reasoned; conclusion still only what the prompt implies).

Driverless cars, against: clear thesis that they should not be manufactured; reasons = liability confusion after accidents, driver inattention, law changes (only 4 states allow semi-autonomous cars), driving becomes boring. org 4 (thesis early, frame complete, all parts on topic, but the four reasons are an interchangeable list - any pair swaps freely); dev 3 (the 4-states figure is the one specific piece and it is dropped in unexplained; the rhetorical questions supporting 'conflict' and 'boring' leave the reader to supply the connection); conv 4 (safetly, 'a nig amount', accented apostrophes - visible but decode instantly; rung 5 fails since the traffic-laws sentence loses control); arg 4 (laziness reason is actually reasoned - drivers assume everything is under control - but no opposing view is engaged and the conclusion only restates the reasons).

Emotion-recognition tech in classrooms: position = the technology is valuable for keeping students from falling behind; support = Prof. Thomas Huang quote (computer recognizes confusion/boredom and modifies the lesson) and the D'Alto zygomatic major/risorius detail showing faked smiles are detectable. org 5 (order is motivated - the fakery paragraph depends on the use case set up before it and explicitly refers back, so no pair swaps without loss; rung 6 fails as no nameable argumentative move is performed by the sequence); dev 5 (both supports specific and attributed, and each explanation adds interpretive work - grade protection, added credibility - but the framing claim about standardized education is unsupported and the second explanation is loose, so not 'every'); conv 3 ('prevent left behind than other students', 'fall credits', fragment 'Which could cause...' - errors accumulate and I re-read to repair, but meaning is recoverable throughout); arg 5 (reasons reasoned, and the anticipated objection that students can hide their feelings is raised and answered, reaching past what the prompt's framing implies; strongest objection - privacy/teacher displacement - is only conceded, so rung 6 fails).

Venus: stance wobbles between 'doesn't sound too bad to think of' and 'no human shoukd go' / 'not a good idea'; content is stitched source facts - Venus is Earth's twin, no spacecraft survived more than a few hours, average over 800 degrees. org 2 (two units only loosely distinguishable, controlling idea must be assembled by the reader and is contradicted across the text; no functioning frame); dev 3 (specific source figures present but they are patchwritten source phrasing lightly stitched, with claims like the Mars comparison unsupported - patchwriting caps here); conv 2 ('That with the author's idea of pursuiting to Venus', the run-on about Mars/neighbors - I had to guess intent more than once, meaning somewhat obscured); arg 2 (a position is stated but vague and self-contradicting, essentially the source handed back with no commitment added).

Seagoing Cowboys: clear position that one should join, three previewed reasons (unique places, adventures, travel if you work). org 4 (thesis early, opening and closing present, all three parts on topic, but they are perfectly interchangeable First/Second/Finally supports); dev 2 (support is circular - 'you can see unique things... visit unique things... find unique stuff'; no named case, figure, or realized example anywhere, only 'taking care of the animals'); conv 4 (typos oceas/slso/becasue/advcentures decode instantly and nothing needs repair, but every sentence is the same shape so rung 5 fails); arg 3 (position clear and committed, but each 'reason' restates the position in other words and the closing circles back to the opening - nothing is reasoned).

Face on Mars: position = a natural landform; support = scientist likening it to Middle Butte in Idaho's Snake River Plain (lava dome/mesa), the pixel-size discernment rule, and the April 5 1998 Mars Global Surveyor photo ten times sharper than Viking. org 5 (order builds - testimony, then the 'scientists can be wrong' doubt answered with the resolution principle, then the sharper photo that the principle licenses; no pair swaps without loss, but the closing only restates so rung 6 fails); dev 4 (support specific throughout and connections stated, but only the pixel-size piece is explained in a way that adds something - the Middle Butte and photo pieces are restated, 'this fact just shows'); conv 4 (missing words 'they know what are doing', 'is actually is indeed a mesa', 'fake' as a wrong-footing word choice - visible, never require re-reading, but control lapses block rung 5); arg 4 (reasons genuinely reasoned via the scientific-reliability move, but the conclusion is one of the two options the prompt's framing already implies, so rung 5 fails).

Driverless cars, one undivided paragraph: opens saying they 'may not be the best thing ever' because kids won't learn to drive, then declares 'im gonna say that the Driverless Cars are good for us', then cheaper ownership, fewer buses/taxis, fewer crashes, an unresolved insurance question. org 2 (a stated position exists but is contradicted by the opening so the reader must assemble it; no functioning frame - ends on an open question - and the units follow with no recoverable relation); dev 2 (support is general throughout - 'gonna help with car crashes', 'itll cost less' - no named case, figure, or realized example); conv 2 ('the way the future is coming to the future vehicals are quite interesting', 'Allowing kids16+ to drive the less crashes will help majorly' - I had to guess intent, meaning somewhat obscured); arg 2 (position stated but vague and self-contradicting, with what look like reasons doing little more than repeating the claim).

Car-free living: opens with questions rather than a stance, then walks through Vauban ($40,000 parking space, 70 percent car-free), the Paris even-plate ban (22-euro fine, 4,000 fined, 67 percent diesel), Bogota's Day Without Cars ($25 fines), and the US driving decline (9 percent below the 2005 peak); position ('every country should have a car-free day') arrives only in the last line. org 3 (controlling idea weakly located - stated late, the intro only poses questions - and the source blocks sit as a survey with the frame perfunctory); dev 3 (figures are plentiful and specific but large stretches reproduce source phrasing lightly stitched with 'the advantage is / a disadvantage is' tags - patchwritten, which caps the trait); conv 2 (in the writer's own sentences - 'driving just means you like your personal things', 'After the smog ruling French party to rescind the ban' - I had to guess, and errors are frequent throughout); arg 2 (no committed stance until a self-cancelling final line, 'it either good or bad'; the essay reports the sources rather than arguing from them).
